sections.value:
PASS -- PR #352 at 7baacf2a468b5441ab947c340e1cd379cf34c77a

One integrated round: correctness, cost, security and privacy. No blocking findings.

Scope: open_assignments queries every open community assignment for the seat across projects and instances, without the context cutoff or a row limit. A released role, including one from an earlier context, does not count as open; a still-open role in another project does. Pods are not implemented at this head (concepts.md:17,60), so there is no separate live pod-member holding path to miss. Role-instance holdings are included. The no-open-role shortcut is limited to --stop; plain close still considers released roles in the current context. A failed open-holdings read cannot select the shortcut.

Notification: context_assignments retains released roles from this context and projects are deduplicated before notification. A held close without a note leaves the seat open. The closer receives the same held FYI and plain-close command, unless it is a notified prime or the target seat. Distinct project primes are notified; a genuinely empty context retains designated-prime fallback. Each not-ready close adds at most one closer FYI, not a wake or a broadcast.

Security: actor resolution, contradictory-attribution refusal and may_close precede the new shortcut. Close still uses the guarded descriptor/prime-authority write. stoppable verifies the recorded PID/start before closing; terminate checks the start again before SIGTERM. A holder needing a turn still encounters the cold-wake guard. No-open-role/no-turn stopping is the explicitly ruled policy, not permission widening. Same-user attacks are out of scope under C33.

Cost: no new loop, poll, timer or process launch; zero new steady-state launches per second, independent of seat/pane count. There is one additional open_assignments helper call per live --stop eligibility decision. Notification replaces an open-holdings query with the existing indexed context lookup (cutoff plus holdings SQL) and adds at most one held FYI to the closer. A roleless stop saves the model turn. The three behavior changes are POLICIES; missing-process and recycled-PID checks remain conservative safety interlocks.

Evidence:
- Exact-head CI run 45548438597 succeeded; headSha is the full reviewed SHA. All five PR checks succeeded. Per packet, CI substitutes for the full local gate; real-tmux tests were not run.
- just pr-freeze 352: FINAL at the reviewed SHA.
- Private exact-head archive: just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --test memory_turn_http --test lifecycle_http --test role_http: 33 + 6 + 14 passed.
- After restoring production source byte-for-byte, the same runner plus four archive-only probes passed: 37 + 6 + 14. The probes covered an open instance holding in another project despite local release, distinct project primes and closer-as-prime deduplication, closer-as-seat deduplication, and release before a delivered compact.
- T1 mutant: tell_primes uses open_assignments instead of context_assignments. The exact T1 failed (exit 101): project prime plain received 0 instead of 1, and designated prime elsewhere received the notice.
- T2 mutant: remove the no-open-role shortcut. The exact T2 failed (exit 101): it returned a memory-turn hold instead of closing/stopping.
- T3 mutant: remove the call.stop condition from the shortcut. The exact T3 failed (exit 101): plain close skipped its required memory turn.

Local mutation builds were serialized through the shared-build lock, with the unchanged 25 GiB floor, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, niceness 19 and four jobs. The detached review worktree was not edited.
